judge.task: ledger-api is a Python web service on PostgreSQL 14 in local development (Docker Compose), CI, and production (Amazon RDS). The scope of this change: AC-001: local development, CI, and production run a supported PostgreSQL major version (PostgreSQL 14 reaches end of life in November 2026). AC-002: developers keep their local data through the change. AC-003: the production upgrade has a tested rollback path; a planned write outage of up to 30 minutes in an announced maintenance window is acceptable, and a rollback is needed only until the upgraded database is verified, before writes resume. The evidence holds the technical design written for this change, which a developer will implement, and any other files that changed. Grade the design.

items.text: Developers' local data reaches the new major version through a dump and restore (for example pg_dump or pg_dumpall, then a restore) or pg_upgrade. FAIL when the design only changes the image tag on the existing data volume, or starts the new version on an empty volume without moving the data.

The local data volume is mounted where the target version's official image keeps its data: /var/lib/postgresql for PostgreSQL 18 and later (the image keeps the data in a version-specific folder below it), or /var/lib/postgresql/data for 17 and earlier. A design that moves to 17 or earlier and keeps the current mount passes. FAIL when the design moves to 18 or later and keeps /var/lib/postgresql/data or does not say where the volume goes, and FAIL when the evidence holds no design that names a target version.
The design moves to PostgreSQL 18 or a later major version, or gives a reason for choosing an older supported one.
Before the upgrade, the design checks whether any role password is stored or checked with MD5 (the production database dates from PostgreSQL 11) and moves those to SCRAM-SHA-256.
Local development, CI, and production all end on the same PostgreSQL major version.
The production upgrade starts with a backup or snapshot and has a rollback path that is tested before the cutover.
